title: ARO Declaration Benchmark — Decoys, Mines, and Camouflaged Troopers

cases.canonicalQuestion: Example a:  I walk past an enemy decoy.   I walk past an enemy Mine at 10 inches away.  I walk past an enemy camo marker that declines to ARO.  Can my opponent say "I do not ARO" with all of those?
cases.approvedAnswer: Yes. “I do not ARO” can mean no AROs are being declared. The reactive player need not identify which marker was eligible. A Decoy replica has no ARO, a real Camouflaged trooper can pass without revealing itself, and an out-of-range Mine does nothing. If an enemy declares or executes a Skill or ARO within a Mine’s Trigger Area and the template can legally be placed, the Mine must trigger.

cases.canonicalQuestion: If all three Decoys stay silent after I Move, does my opponent have to point out which one could ARO?
cases.approvedAnswer: No. A Decoy replica has no ARO to declare. The real trooper can decline an eligible ARO without revealing itself, so a general “no ARO” does not identify the real trooper. If the real trooper passes when first eligible, it forfeits the ARO for that Order unless a rule specifically allows it to delay.

cases.canonicalQuestion: My Move passes through a Mine's Trigger Area and the template is legal. Does it still go off if the defender says no ARO?
cases.approvedAnswer: Yes. A deployed Mine must trigger when an enemy Model or Marker declares or executes a Skill or ARO inside its Trigger Area, provided the template can legally be placed. A blanket “no ARO” does not waive that trigger. The Mine cannot trigger if the template would affect an ally, and Total Cover from the Blast Focus is outside its Trigger Area.

cases.canonicalQuestion: If I stay at least ten inches from the Mine for my entire Move, does it trigger?
cases.approvedAnswer: No. If the entire Move is outside the Mine's Trigger Area, the Mine does not trigger. The trigger is checked against the Mine's Small Teardrop Template, not a trooper's Zone of Control. Check the path as well as the endpoint.

cases.canonicalQuestion: A real camo trooper has LoF to my first Move and says no ARO. Can it shoot after my second Move in the same Order?
cases.approvedAnswer: No. If the CAMO trooper already had a valid ARO after the first Short Skill and passed, it forfeits the ARO against that Order. Merely passing does not reveal it. A trooper that first becomes eligible after the second Short Skill can react then. An explicit rule allowing a delay is separate from passing.

cases.canonicalQuestion: My first Move gives the CAMO trooper no valid ARO. My second Move gives it LoF for the first time and its first valid ARO. Can it react after saying no ARO earlier?
cases.approvedAnswer: Yes. If the trooper had no valid ARO after the first Short Skill and the second Short Skill grants its first valid ARO, it can react then. A blanket “no ARO” at the first window does not give up an ARO that was not yet available.
